description: 5P468-26-0151/A Stage 2 -Amishku-Shipiss-Kigiap Konga - Beaver Brook Camp-Akami-Uapishk?-KakKasuak-Mealy Mountains National Park Reserve REQUIREMENT The Beaver Brook Camp project involves the complete construction of a camp facility located at the junction of Lake Melville and Etagaulet River, in Newfoundland and Labrador (Approx. coordinates are: 53°42'56.37"N 59°01'06.20"W). The Camp is comprised of 3 buildings, a Lodge (69m2 with a 34m2 screen porch and deck), a Privy (Backcountry Toilet, approx. 18m2) and a Cache (Storage Shed, approx. 25m2), all linked through wooden boardwalks (approx. 250m of boardwalks) and powered through solar panels. Tent Pads (five (5) total), a food cache, a seasonal floating dock, log benches, picnic tables, fire pit and a traditional camping site are also included in this project. Overall site work, tree clearing, topsoil preservation and re-naturalization, is required for this site. The site is remote with no existing infrastructure and is only accessible by boat, seaplane, helicopter or by snowmobile (during winter-pending safe ice conditions). TWO STAGE SELECTION PROCESS This posting is the Stage Two of a two-stage solicitation process: the first stage was to evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers. The second stage (Stage Two) is to invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings. Only qualified suppliers have been invited to bid. Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business”

Sopimuskaudet 2+1+1., ARK ja PS suunnittelupalvelut Tilaajan kiinteistöjen rakennussuunnittelun asiantuntijapalvelut sisältäen seuraavat tehtävät: Suunnittelutehtävään sisältyvät arkkitehti- ja pääsuunnittelutehtävät Arkkitehtisuunnittelun tehtäväluettelon ARK18 (RT 103253) sekä Pääsuunnittelun tehtäväluettelon PS18 (RT 103254) mukaisessa laajuudessa., RAK suunnittelupalvelut Rakennesuunnittelijan tehtävät Tehtäviin kuuluu rakennesuunnittelun työtehtävät Rakennesuunnittelun tehtäväluettelon RAK 18 mukaisesti., Sähkösuunnittelun palvelut Sähkösuunnittelijan tehtävät Tehtäviin kuuluu sähkösuunnittelun työtehtävät. title: Anskaffelse av løsning for backup og reservedrift
description: Plan- og bygningsetaten forvalter store mengder data knyttet til byggesaker, eiendom, geodata og mer. Stabil tilgang til disse dataene er avgjørende for å sikre effektiv saksbehandling og leveranse av tjenester til innbyggere og næringsliv. Anskaffelsens formål er å etablere en sikker og robust løsning for sikkerhetskopiering og gjenoppretting av data. Løsningen som anskaffes skal bidra til å sikre høy tilgjengelighet til etatens data og systemer og redusere risiko knyttet til tap av data, sikkerhetshendelser og driftsavbrudd. Løsningen skal understøtte etatens behov for: - beskyttelse av virksomhetskritiske data - rask gjenoppretting ved hendelser - robusthet mot cybertrusler (herunder ransomware) - fleksibilitet i forbindelse med overgang til Oslo kommunes felles IKT-plattform Anskaffelsen omfatter en samlet løsning for backup og gjenoppretting som kan bestå av: - tjenesteleveranse fra leverandørens plattform - drift av løsninger i kundens eller tredjeparts miljø - nødvendige komponenter for lagring og gjenoppretting Løsningen skal sikre at sikkerhetskopier lagres på minst to uavhengige lokasjoner, som er fysisk og logisk adskilt.

title: Finland – Wide area network services – Tietoliikennepalvelut ja valokuituverkon myynti
description: Hankintayksikkö pyytää tarjousta seuraavasta palvelukokonaisuudesta: • Tietoliikenneverkko sekä tähän liittyviä optioita. Toimittajan tulee tarjota kokonaisuutta. Osatarjouksia ei hyväksytä. Vaihtoehtoisia tarjouksia ei hyväksytä. Kyseisen kokonaisuuden tarkemmat tiedot ja tarjousvaatimukset löytyvät tarjouspyynnön liitteestä 1, jossa on ilmoitettu tarjottavien palveluiden vähimmäis- ja laatuvaatimukset. Osana hankintaa myydään Tilaajan omistaman kuituverkon yhteyksiä Toimittajalle. Toimittaja ilmoittaa hintaliitteellä hinnan, jonka se kuituverkosta maksaa Tilaajalle. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin, koska kyseessä on tekninen ja toiminnallinen kokonaisuus, jonka jakaminen osiin muodostaisi Tilaajalle merkittävän teknisen ja toiminnallisen riskin sekä saattaisi merkittävästi haitata kriittisten tietoliikenneyhteyksien saatavuutta tulevaisuudessa. Hankinnassa noudatetaan hankintalakia (1397/2016). Menettelytapana on EU kynnysarvon ylittävä avoin menettely. Tarjouspyyntöasiakirjat ovat suomen kielellä ja tarjous tulee antaa suomen kielellä. Tarjoajan tulee huomioida, että hankinta-asiakirjojen saantia on rajoitettu hankintalain 69.3 §:n perusteella: Kaikkia hankinta-asiakirjoja ei voida asettaa rajoituksetta, suoraan ja kokonaan sähköisessä muodossa saataville tietojen luottamuksellisuuden suojaamiseksi. Tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoihin liittyy salassa pidettävää aineistoa (Tarjouspyynnön liite 4 - Kohdeluettelo). Menettelyohjeet salassapidettävän materiaalin saamiseksi on ilmoitettu hankintailmoituksen kohdassa: "Hankintaa tai osaa koskevat lisätiedot". Learnpoint ICT Oy toimii hankinnassa konsulttina.

title: Design – Marsh Viewing Tower, Point Pelee National Park
description: BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to bid solicitations is soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca. Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT Parks Canada Agency (PCA) is seeking the services of a structural engineering firm recognized and licensed to practice in Ontario with experience in viewing tower design and construction. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than two (2) calendar days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. title: RF Data Fusion for Command and Control
description: This Challenge notice is issued under the Innovation for Defence Excellence and Security (IDEaS) Program Call for Proposals (CFP) Call 006 (W7714-248676/A). Solicitation Documents reference: See bidding details section. *For additional general information on the IDEaS Program, visit: https://www.canada.ca/en/department-national-defence/programs/defence-ideas.html _____________ This challenge is open to receive proposals for Component 1a, Component 1b and Component 2. Proposed solutions that fall within technology readiness levels (TRL) 1-9 can be submitted to this challenge. Steps to apply: Step 1: read this challenge Step 2: read the Call for Proposals : See bidding details section Step 3: propose your solution here : https://defence-innovation-portal.my.site.com/ _____________ Maximum Funding and Performance Period Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. The individual maximum contract funding available under Component 1a (TRL 1-3) is up to $250,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of up to 6 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 1b (TRL 4-5) is up to $1,500,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes) for a maximum performance period of 12 months. The maximum individual contract funding available under Component 2 (TRL 6-9) is up to $5,000,000 CAD (excluding applicable taxes). The period of performance will be determined at the time of contract negotiation. The maximum individual contractual funding and the maximum performance period offered under Component 3 will be determined by Canada at the time of contract negotiation. This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to contract for the total approximate funding. _____________ Challenge Details Challenge Title: W7714-248676/017 - RF Data Fusion for Command and Control The Department of National Defence (DND) and the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) are seeking innovative software-based solutions to seamlessly convert, analyze, and fuse real-time, domain-specific, content-rich data transmitted over radio frequency (RF) bearers into a secure, standardized pan-domain Command and Control (C2) format to enhance interoperability and enable timely, data-driven decision-making across all domains and levels of command. Background and context Radio frequency (RF) communications in military operations are inherently bandwidth-constrained and vulnerable to jamming, interference, and environmental effects, making them unreliable in contested environments. To maintain timely and effective support across all warfighting domains, data transmitted over RF bearers should be transformed into compact, structured messages, such as eXtensible Markup Language (XML)-based Message Text Formats (MTF) or other machine-readable schemas. Such messages should be optimized for transmission over tactical networks including Low Frequency (LF), Very Low Frequency (VLF), High Frequency (HF), Ultra High Frequency (UHF), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM). This approach enables resilient, standards-based communication across domains (land, air, maritime, cyber, and space) and functional services (e.g., Joint Intelligence Surveillance and Reconnaissance (JISR), medical, logistics), in line with doctrinal requirements for pan-domain operations. CAF tactical messaging remains largely dependent on legacy systems. These systems are inflexible, poorly suited to machine-to-machine exchange, and increasingly misaligned with NATO’s shift toward XML-based, data-centric frameworks. CAF operators currently lack integrated, machine-readable messaging systems. As a result, they must manually convert voice, chat, and text inputs into formal military products including orders, situation reports, and Requests for Information (RFIs) to comply with command structures and coalition standards. Modern, pan-domain operations require that doctrinal and technical Information Exchange Requirements (IERs) be met at the speed of operational relevance, with messaging that is interoperable, standardized, and capable of supporting real-time, data-driven decision-making in joint and coalition environments. As NATO, the U.S. Department of Defense, and other Five Eyes partners adopt XML-based, machine-readable messaging frameworks, the CAF is prioritizing alignment with these emerging data models to improve interoperability, operational agility, and mission effectiveness. The DND/CAF are seeking innovative, interoperable, and scalable solutions that will contribute to the development of a next-generation digital military RF messaging and data exchange. Innovators are invited to propose technologies, platforms, or integrated systems. Essential Outcomes The proposed solution must: • Be a software-based capability (e.g., standalone application, plug-in, middleware, or service). • Support DND/CAF operations across all domains (land, air, maritime, space, cyber) and functional services (e.g., C2, intelligence, logistics). • Implement structured, standards-compliant messaging (e.g., MTF-XML) and data exchange protocols (e.g., National Information Exchange Model (NIEM), NATO Core Data Framework (NCDF)), with documented interfaces for importing, exporting, and exchanging data using those standards. • Be configurable and modular, supporting Character-Oriented Information Exchange (COIE) processing and designed for future extensibility (e.g., to accommodate emerging or disruptive standards). • Provide documented interfaces and standards-based data exchange mechanisms to support system integration, including use within experimentation, simulation, and wargaming environments. Desired Outcomes The proposed solution should include capabilities such as, but not limited to, the following: • Operability in Denied, Degraded, Intermittent, and Low Bandwidth (DDIL) environments, with scalability to support evolving mission requirements and force structures. • Enhanced user experience features such as intuitive interfaces, multilingual support, automation of routine workflows, and built-in decision aids. • Standardized, documented integration interfaces (e.g., application programming interfaces (APIs)) to enable integration with at least one Service Management or Service Monitoring tools or platforms (e.g., ServiceNow, Splunk, Dynatrace, Microsoft System Center, Azure Monitor, etc.). • Readiness for future integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) capabilities to support data fusion, intelligent message prioritization, and real-time decision support.

description: This project involves replacing the existing fire alarm system at the Sir Frederick Banting Building with a new fully addressable, networked fire alarm system while maintaining continuous building operations and fire protection throughout construction. The work includes installing new fire alarm equipment, devices, wiring, and controls; integrating the system with elevators, HVAC equipment, electromagnetic locks, fire protection systems, emergency generators, and the monitoring station; and completing all required testing, verification, commissioning, and code compliance activities. Once the new system is operational and accepted, the existing fire alarm infrastructure will be removed and all affected areas restored. The work will be carried out in phases within an occupied laboratory and office facility, requiring careful coordination to minimize disruptions and maintain life-safety functions at all times.

title: SPS-02357 Temporary Maintenance Staff
description: The SPS has a number of facilities containing buildings and equipment which are required to be inspected, serviced and maintained. This work is carried out by the Estates and Technical Services Directorate managed by SPS Headquarters (HQ). SPS currently operates 14 publicly managed prisons, two Community Custody Units (CCUs), its HQ, the SPS College, and a Central Stores facility, all situated across Scotland. This framework shall provide SPS with the capability to employ suitably qualified and experienced temporary staff, covering a range of skill sets required in maintenance services. The supplier shall be able to provide temporary staff to the SPS sites across Scotland and the level of service shall be consistent.

title: USMCFP SPRINGFIELD - Bio-Medical Waste Removal
description: Completed SF1449 is required with bid and bid must be within spec of the Statement of Work to be considered. USMCFP SPRINGFIELD MEDICAL WASTE DISPOSAL: STATEMENT OF WORK Subject The Federal Bureau of Prisons intends to make a single award to a responsible entity for the provision of Medical Waste Disposal for USMCFP Springfield. Medical Waste Disposal services shall only be used for medical hazardous waste that cannot be disposed of with garbage removed by the standard trash service. This contract is for Medical Waste Disposal that will need to be provided every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday throughout the contract. Place of Performance Services for Medical Waste Disposal will be performed at the address 1900 W Sunshine St. Springfield, Missouri 65807. There is a commercial entrance off Sunshine Steet to access the property. The driver will proceed to the talk box and receive directions from the officer. There is a small structure that houses medical waste. Period of Performance USMCFP Springfield is soliciting for a 12-month period of performance to start date of award and end 12 months after date of award with a 6-month option to extend to 18 months after date of original award. Schedule The contractor shall pick up Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays for the duration of the contract. Any deviation from this schedule will be mutually agreed upon by the Contractor and the Government. There will be no pickups on federal holidays. Pickups scheduled for federal holidays will be rescheduled for the next business day. Note: Three pickups will be required each week per policy. The time of pick up will be from 7:30 am to 10:30 am or 11:30 am to 2:30 pm. Licensing Requirements The institution requires all applicable Federal, EPA, and Missouri licensing / regulations that are standard for this industry. Service must also comply with the Disposal of Patient Materials standards which I have attached below: Security Clearance Services will be provided outside the secured confines of the institution. Please see the Terms and Conditions for any further requirements. Description of Duties The objective of this contract is to provide Medical Waste Disposal for USMCFP Springfield. The contractor shall be responsible for, but is not limited to, the following: The contractor shall be responsible for the collection, removal, and disposal of infectious medical waste. These duties must be in accordance with all Federal, State, City ordinances, laws, and regulations. Containers to furnish will be red, reusable plastic tubs with lid with overall dimensions of not to exceed (24x24x24 inches). Preferably 31 Gallon in size tubs. Tub liners and tape will be furnished by the contractor and appropriately supplied with each pickup. The contractor will leave an appropriate number of tubs and lids to exchange upon request. This includes providing properly sanitized tubs and lids. The contractor holder will determine an appropriate quantity of tubs to have on hand. On average 8 full tubs will be picked up Monday�s and Wednesday�s. Fridays will average 16-20 full tubs. The estimated medical waste to be removed is 85,000 lbs per year. Only the actual weight of waste collected will be billed. Disposal charge does not include the weight of the reusable tubs or lids. Electronic manifest is preferred Each Invoice will contain: Date of pickup, number of pickups, total weight of waste picked up, pricing according to the contract mirroring the line items on the contract. Point of Contact Contractor shall provide a Point of Contact (POC) who shall be responsible for the delivery of the services under this contract. The POC shall have the full authority to act on behalf of the contractor on all matters relating to the daily operation of the contracted services. The contractor shall designate this individual, in writing, to the Contracting Officer (CO) prior to contract start date. An alternate may be designated; however, the contractor must identify those times when the alternate shall be the primary POC. English Language Requirements The contractor performing the services under this contractual agreement shall have the ability to read, understand, fluently speak and legibly write in the English language. Government Quality Assurance The Government reserves the right to inspect and evaluate all services provided during the performance under this contract. All observations will be documented by the designated Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). When an observation indicates defective performance, the Contracting Officer, along with the support of the COR, may issue a Discrepancy Report to the contractor. The contractor shall address any Discrepancy Report in writing to the COR and the Contracting Officer, within ten (10) calendar days of notification indicating any corrective action to be taken to rectify the deficiency. Non-Personal Services Information The service is a contractual arrangement and not a personnel appointment. Payment is based on the provision of an end product or the accomplishment of a specific result. The service does not constitute an employer/employee relationship.

description: RFQ Amendment 0004 has been posted below. Furthermore, industry questions and answers are forthcoming based on the questions received from industry. NOTE: PLEASE BE ADVISED BEGINNING MONDAY, AUGUST 17, 2026 TRAVEL RESTIRICTIONS BEGIN AROUND THE RONALD REGAN BUILDING DUE TO THE PREPARATION FOR THE GRAND PRIX RACE. PLEASE ACCOUNT FOR POTENTIAL TRAVEL DELAY AND ALLOW ADDITONAL TRAVEL TIME TO ATTEND THE SITE VISIT SCHEDULED FOR MONDAY, AUGUST 17, 2026 AT 10AM ET. The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Federal Protective Service (FPS) has a requirement for corrective and preventative maintenance of electronic security systems and the replacement and removal of outdated electronic security systems at the Ronald Reagan Building (DC0459). The Contractor shall provide preventive maintenance, repair, replacement, lifecycle upgrades and installations to meet assessed security vulnerabilities / gaps in existing security systems. The services include, but are not limited to, routine and preventive maintenance, repairs and service calls. The VSS equipment includes, interior and exterior fixed IP cameras, controllers, monitors and NVR recorders, power supplies, and all associated ancillary equipment and infrastructure that are part of the Ronald Reagan Building Complex. The Period of Performance is for a one-year base ordering period with four one-year optional ordering periods. An Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with fixed priced provisions is anticipated. This acquisition is being solicited as a total Women-Owned Small Business set aside. Resultant task orders under this contract will be firm fixed price. The source selection process to be utilized for this acquisition is best value/trade-off. The technical, non-price factor, when combined, is more important than price. The submission requirements and evaluation criteria will be defined in the solicitation. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 561621 with size standard is $25 million. The successful Contractor is required to be register with the System for Award Management (SAM) at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for award. All questions must be submitted in writing to Contract Specialist Christopher Kelly at Christopher.Kelly@fps.dhs.gov.

title: Kingdom of Bahrain S&RTS
description: The purpose of this requirement is to provide S&RTS in connection with the import and export of designated U.S. Government (USG) cargo throughout the Kingdom of Bahrain. Primary performance locations include Mina Salman Port, Khalifa Bin Salman Port, ASRY Dry Dock, Naval Support Activity (NSA1), Mina Salman Naval Base (NSA2), Shaikh Isa Air Base, Aviation Unit (NSA3), Riffa Air Base and any other designated locations within Kingdom of Bahrain. S&RTS services will cover the full spectrum of managing USG cargo (e.g. containers, vehicles, breakbulk, and rotary or fixed wing aircraft) transiting through the specified port(s) in this contract. Operational tasks shall include but are not limited to stevedoring and long-shoring services required to conduct and facilitate load and discharge of vessel, truck, port reception and disposition, cargo management and preparation, staging, storage, onward movement, intra-port transfers, vessel preparation, documentation, tallying and checking, and storage of dunnage and tiedown materials. Military cargo may consist of vehicles, Ammunition and Explosives (A&E) in all sizes and configurations (containerized or breakbulk), non-explosive containers of all sizes, all classes of Hazardous Materials (HAZMAT) (IAW applicable regulations), and other general DoW cargo. Transportation will be facilitated via vessel, Common-User Land Transportation (CULT), and/or military convoy.

description: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation FA8224-27-Q-0001 Portable Fire Extinguisher & Fire Suppression System Services For the benefit of AMXG, Hill AFB, UT This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with RFO Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number FA8224-27-Q-0001 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ) for monthly and annual inspection, maintenance, and monitoring of portable fire extinguishers, and annual fire suppression system inspection located within AMXG facilities at Hill AFB, Utah. As provided in the attached statement of work, all work on this contract shall comply with applicable federal, state, local, and Hill AFB fire prevention regulations It is the Government�s intention to establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) with a single entity for a one-year period with four additional option years. The Government is obligated only to the extent of authorized purchases actually made under the BPA by an authorized individual, and then only when performance of services has been made and accepted by the Government. All qualified sources are encouraged to submit a quote which will be considered by the agency. Contractors must provide proof of valid and active licensing issued by the Utah State Fire Marshal for servicing portable fire extinguishers as well as fire suppression systems. Contractor personnel must possess an active certification of registration by the Utah State Fire Marshal at time of service. Contractors must be registered at SAM.gov and have an active CAGE code at the time of response. A company that is not registered in SAM.gov or which does not possess an active CAGE code may contact APEX Accelerators for assistance in completing the registration process. A document with the APEX Accelerators contact information is included in this solicitation. Respondents to this solicitation shall specify whether the entity is a large business, 8(a) concern, women-owned small business, HUBZone small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business. Respondents must also specify whether they are a U.S.-owned or foreign-owned firm. This acquisition is 100% set-aside for small business concerns. To be considered a small business for this solicitation a company�s annual revenue may not exceed $25M. The NAICS Code for this solicitation is 561621. The provision at RFO 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors � Commercial Products and Commercial Services, applies to this acquisition. Quotations are due by Noon Mountain Daylight Saving Time on Friday, 30 October 2026 via electronic mail to ammon.helms@us.af.mil. Quoters are responsible for verifying receipt of Quote. Oral quotes will not be accepted. To be considered for award. Quoters are responsible for including the following eight items in their response: The solicitation number The name, address, telephone number of the Quoter A CAGE code and active SAM.gov Unique Entity ID. An active Portable Fire Extinguisher Company Privilege License Number issued by the Utah State Fire Marshal. An active Fire Suppression Systems Company Privilege License Number issued by the Utah State Fire Marshal. A company profile and capabilities statement that may not exceed one single-sided, letter-sized page. Completed FA8224-27-Q-0001 Pricing Response Form An affirmative statement specifying the extent of agreement with all terms, conditions, and provisions included in the solicitation and any solicitation amendments. description: This is a sources sought notice. Under the JIT delivery method, the Medical Treatment Facility (MTF) calls the manufacturer�s field representative who carriers the products into the MTF just-in-time for the surgery. At the request of the MTFs, the manufacturer is required to have a qualified representative on site at the MTFs within the timeframe specified by the facility necessary to meet their requirements. The project consists of replacing the existing bridge with a new fixed bridge on a new alignment and to provide for partial demolition of the existing bridge. The new fixed bridge will be a single-span steel girder bridge with a concrete deck. The bridge width will be 34�4�� out-to-out, with two 11�0� travel lanes, two 2�0� shoulders, a 5�0� sidewalk, and the superstructure will consist of four (4) built-up steel plate girders. The replacement bridge alignment is located immediately downstream of the existing bridge and, at its northern terminus, will fit entirely between the existing bridge and the Bonneville Power Administration transmission tower which is located to the south. Approach roadways will also be constructed to tie into the existing roadway alignment. The new fixed bridge will be located over the existing navigation channel and will provide an under clearance that is larger than is currently present under the existing bridge. The north abutment will be a concrete stub abutment with spread footing anchored into rock. The south abutment will be a concrete abutment that is supported by drilled shafts. To mitigate seismic hazards, portions of the existing bridge will be removed as part of the bridge construction requirement. The existing bridge provides for critical vehicular access to the Bonneville project that must remain open for the entirety of the construction project. This will likely require the contractor to construct the project in phases. In addition, lead and asbestos removal will be required as part of this requirement. title: Head Start in State Systems Sole Source Award
description: This requirement was awarded through task order 47QRAA-20D-001M/7571MN26F80105 This requirement will support the generation and dissemination of research and/or evaluation that builds on the Financing Early Care and Education (ECE) Study task order (47QRAA-20D-001M/ 140D0422F0154). The primary objective is to generate and disseminate evidence pertaining to the financing of early care and education programs that meet child, family, and community needs. Building on data collected under the prior contract, this project will identify and elevate strategies used to align Head Start programs within state funding contexts to reduce administrative burden and expand the reach of ECE and Head Start funding. The research will focus on how Head Start programs operate within state systems and highlight effective strategies states have used to integrate or build upon Head Start funding within their broader early childhood systems. The project will also examine how efforts to streamline licensing and regulatory requirements, workforce standards, and supports for quality and technical assistance across funding streams can reduce burden, improve program efficiency, increase parental access to ECE, and support child and family outcomes. This requirement will build on prior efforts to identify and elevate financing approaches for states that most effectively align funding streams to both reduce burden and increase the reach of ECE funding. This project will provide ACF with critical evidence to understand how federal early care and education programs can achieve the Agency�s mission and vision of (1) supporting federalism & local leadership by providing actionable insights into how states and localities can leverage Head Start and other federal funding streams for early care and education (ECE) to best meet local needs, (2) promoting quality early learning environments and improved child outcomes by understanding how to leverage existing funding sources to best meet the preferences of families with young children consistent with their unique needs, and (3) promoting work and self-sufficiency by exploring how leveraging funds can expand the availability of ECE services that allow parents to work.

description: Pre-Solicitation Conference � NSWCPD Environmental Qualification Test Services The Naval Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) invites interested contractors to a pre-solicitation conference regarding the future requirement for Testing Services in support of Shock and Vibration and Electromagnetic Interference / Compatibility (EMI/EMC) Environmental Qualification efforts for Navy Hull, Mechanical, and Electrical (HME) equipment. PSC Code: Z2AA NAICS Code: 236220 Small Business Size Standard: $45M Description: This is a Multiple Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract that provides for an indefinite quantity of supplies or services during a fixed period. The GSA intends to award multiple contracts for General Construction Services. After award of the IDIQ all awardees will be provided fair opportunity in accordance with FAR 16.507-2 for discrete construction projects where a single task order will be issued based on selection criteria established at the ordering level, unless an exemption exists in accordance with FAR 16.507-6. The General Contractor (GC) shall serve as the single point of responsibility and must supervise, administer, coordinate, perform, and contract all management, labor, materials, equipment, and construction activities required to successfully execute each assigned project. Construction services will be required to be performed at federally owned and leased locations. The operational scope encompasses comprehensive general construction, repair, alteration, and modernization services for existing real property facilities. The General Contractor (GC) shall supervise, administer, perform, and contract all construction activities required to complete a project. Construction services include, but are not limited to office construction and/or renovations/repairs, office space renovations, MEP (Mechanical/Electrical/Plumbing) repairs/modifications/replacement, fire sprinkler systems repairs/modification/replacement, sitework, exterior construction repair and alterations (including facades and roofs), demolition (including abatement of hazardous materials), elevator modernizations, work in technically sensitive environments like laboratories, SCIF�s etc., work in high-security data centers and critical infrastructure control systems, construction work in high security buildings, as well as any other general construction activities. title: Encroachment Management Implementation and Mission Readiness, Sustainment, and Compatibility Services AE IDIQ, Unrestricted
description: THIS IS AN UNRESTRICTED PROCUREMENT. This procurement will result in one Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract for multi-discipline Architect-Engineer (A-E) services for Encroachment Management Implementation and Mission Readiness, Sustainment, and Compatibility services at various Navy and Marine Corps installations primarily in the Navy Region Southwest but may also include work worldwide. These services will be procured in accordance with 40 USC Chapter 11, Selection of Architects and Engineers, as implemented by FAR 36. The IDIQ contract will be for a base period of two (2) years and three (3) one-year option periods (if exercised). The total fee for the contract term shall not exceed $30,000,000. The guaranteed minimum for the contract term (including option years) is $1,000. Firm-fixed price task orders will be negotiated for this contract. The minimum value of individual task orders executed under this contract is $25,000. The maximum value of individual task orders executed under this contract is $2,500,000. There will be no dollar limit per year. Estimated start date is March 2027. The Small Business size standard classification is North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code 541330 (Engineering Services). The Government seeks the most highly qualified firm to perform the required services, based on the demonstrated competence and qualifications, in accordance with the selection criteria. Primary A-E Services: 1. Land Use Planning. 2. Air Installations Compatible Use Zones (AICUZ) and Range Air Installations Compatible Use Zones (RAICUZ) Studies. 3. Encroachment Action Plans (EAP) or Encroachment Control Plans (ECP). 4. Strategic Engagement and Communication Plans (SECP). 5. Outreach Planning Materials. 6. Electronic Database. Secondary Services: 1. Other related studies/analysis: Provide additional services to assist in implementation of encroachment management studies, Range Complex Management Plans (RCMP), Integrated Natural Resource Management Plans (INRMP), Readiness and Environmental Protection Integration (REPI) Program plans, and other special planning, engineering, and encroachment support deliverables, such as analytical assessments, geospatial analysis and simulations, traffic studies, glint/glare analysis, radar assessments, plume analysis and modeling, lighting studies, and socio-economic studies. 2. Other Related Reports or Documentation: Deliverables also include assistance with incidental services related to providing public notice for studies and publicizing and providing training on encroachment-related studies. Please see attached synopsis for full synopsis description/instructions.

title: Sea Range Safety Surveillance Services
description: 1) INTRODUCTION AND PURPOSE: NAWCWD is seeking technically competent sources for engineering services in support of Test and Evaluation (T&E) and systems engineering activities related to Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) and Theater High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) programs at Pacific Missile Range Facility (PMRF). The purpose of this sources sought is to determine what companies are capable of providing the required services in a competitive procurement and to gain market knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classifications relative to the North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code 541330 for Engineering Services which has a corresponding size standard of $47 million. Responses to this sources sought synopsis will be utilized by the Government to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement and make appropriate determinations about potential sources. No solicitation is currently available and as such this is not a request for proposal and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. A decision to set aside all or part of this requirement is dependent upon a review of the information submitted in response to this sources sought. After review of responses to this sources sought, a synopsis and/or solicitation announcement may be published. (2) PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: This requirement is for engineering services to be provided in support of Test and Evaluation (T&E) and systems engineering activities primarily related to Aegis-Based Defense, formerly Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) and Sea-Based Weapon Systems. Engineering service are provided to other entities, including (but not limited to) Program Executive Office Integrated Warfare Systems (PEO IWS), various Hypersonic programs, and Allied Foreign Military Sales (FMS) partners. Aegis-Based Defense is one weapon system in the layered defense provided for the United States and its deployed forces, friends and allies against ballistic missiles of all ranges in all phases of flight. This defense is provided through an integrated Ballistic Missile Defense System (BMDS), developed by the Missile Defense Agency (MDA). MDA is responsible for fulfilling the goals set out in the National Missile Defense Act of 1999 in deploying �as soon as is technologically possible an effective National Missile Defense system capable of defending the territory of the United States against limited ballistic missile attack�. In support of this goal, the Aegis-Based Defense program needs to collect high fidelity system under test and auxiliary sensor data in order to evaluate the results of the flight test and to determine if the system(s) met the mission objectives. Additionally, auxiliary sensor data is highly valuable in providing forensics for any anomalies that may have occurred during these events. Pre-/post-mission data analyses of this auxiliary sensor data is critical these flight test scenarios. This is a follow-on contract to N6893622D0024. The existing contract is Cost-Plus Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Level of Effort (LOE), and was awarded to Raytheon (RTX) on a sole source basis. The new contract will be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP). (3) REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: The MDA / Aegis-Based Defense program requires high fidelity pre-mission planning, real-time mission conduct and execution support, post-mission data analysis, and reporting of test results of high profile flight test events. Support shall be provided to various flight test events and systems engineering activities. This includes mission planning, test planning, generating test procedures, real-time mission conduct, data collection, real-time range safety mission support, mission data analyses and reporting, operations research support, and technical management support. Aegis-Based Defense requires support for test planning, test conduct, data reduction/analysis, and reporting of auxiliary sensor data during flight test events. This includes in-depth pre-mission analysis, which provides inputs to instrumentation, sensor data collection CONOPS, and sensor configurations to maximize valuable data collection. Recommendations for test support positions (TSPs) to auxiliary sensors will aid in maximizing valuable data collected. Inputs to test plans as well as mission requirements are needed to ensure mission test objectives are met. This includes auxiliary tracking and data collection objectives based on mission priorities and overall test objectives. Understanding test objectives will translate directly into what instrumentation should be used and how they should be configured. This includes inputs to all test participants (sea-based, ground-based, airborne, and space-based). Real-time mission conduct support assists auxiliary sensor participants to make adjustments to configurations, tracking objectives, and/or tracking CONOPS based on changes to mission scenarios. This support can ensure successful data collection during live missile and test vehicle launches. Mission conduct and execution support includes providing sensor and analysis support to assist range safety. Complex analyses and reporting of test results is needed to evaluate weapons and weapon systems to ensure mission test objectives have been met. This includes ingesting, reducing, processing, and analyzing all auxiliary data (optical, radar, telemetry) and data formats. Analyses and test results should be shared with the government and test community to ensure proper communication and collaboration. (4) PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: This effort will primarily be performed at PMRF at Barking Sands, Kauai, HI. Support will also be conducted at the following national test ranges and locations: Joint Base Pearl Harbor Hickam (JBPHH) on Oahu, HI; Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division (NAWCWD) Point Mugu Sear Range (PMSR) at Point Mugu, CA; Vandenberg Space Force Base (SFB) in CA; Reagan Test Site (RTS) on Kwajalein Atoll; Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER) in AK; Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS) at Cape Canaveral, FL; Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) at Patuxent River, MD; and the Missile Defense Integration and Operations Center (MDIOC) at Colorado Springs, CO. (5) CONTRACT TYPE: The Government is considering a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) Idefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with a five-year Ordering Period. title: Aegis Based Defense Engineering Services
description: 1) INTRODUCTION AND PURPOSE: NAWCWD is seeking technically competent sources for engineering services in support of Test and Evaluation (T&E) and systems engineering activities related to Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) and Theater High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) programs at Pacific Missile Range Facility (PMRF). The purpose of this sources sought is to determine what companies are capable of providing the required services in a competitive procurement and to gain market knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classifications relative to the North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code 541330 for Engineering Services which has a corresponding size standard of $47 million. Responses to this sources sought synopsis will be utilized by the Government to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement and make appropriate determinations about potential sources. No solicitation is currently available and as such this is not a request for proposal and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. A decision to set aside all or part of this requirement is dependent upon a review of the information submitted in response to this sources sought. After review of responses to this sources sought, a synopsis and/or solicitation announcement may be published. (2) PROGRAM DESCRIPTION: This requirement is for engineering services to be provided in support of Test and Evaluation (T&E) and systems engineering activities primarily related to Aegis-Based Defense, formerly Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense (BMD) and Sea-Based Weapon Systems. Engineering service are provided to other entities, including (but not limited to) Program Executive Office Integrated Warfare Systems (PEO IWS), various Hypersonic programs, and Allied Foreign Military Sales (FMS) partners. Aegis-Based Defense is one weapon system in the layered defense provided for the United States and its deployed forces, friends and allies against ballistic missiles of all ranges in all phases of flight. This defense is provided through an integrated Ballistic Missile Defense System (BMDS), developed by the Missile Defense Agency (MDA). MDA is responsible for fulfilling the goals set out in the National Missile Defense Act of 1999 in deploying �as soon as is technologically possible an effective National Missile Defense system capable of defending the territory of the United States against limited ballistic missile attack�. title: Germany – Lift installation work – Modernisierung GS Dorschbergschule - Aufzüge
description: Die Grundschule Dorschberg in Wörth a. Rh. wurde 1966 baulich errichtet und liegt hinter dem Mittelbau der Carl–Benz–Gesamtschule in Wörth am Rhein. Die Grundschule besteht aus vier Gebäudeteilen, zu welchen ein ein- bzw. zweigeschossiger Gebäudeteil mit Verbindungsgängen gehört sowie eine Pausenhalle mit einem Verwaltungstrakt und einem eingeschossigen Pavillonbau mit vier Pavillongebäuden. Die Gebäude sind mit Pausengängen verbunden und verfügen über zwei Toilettengebäude. Die ein- bis zweigeschossigen Gebäude wurden in massiver Bauweise mit Beton-Fertigteilen errichtet und weisen Flachdächer in unterschiedlichen Höhenlagen mit umlaufender Attika auf und wurden bis heute mehrfach saniert und modernisiert. Mitte der 1990er Jahre fand eine Betonsanierung statt. In diesem Zuge wurde ein Wärmedämm-Verbundsystem und die Alucobond-Verkleidungen der Attiken und der Fertigteilstützen angebracht. Wesentliche bauliche Maßnahmen - Der bestehende eingeschossige Klassentrakt wird aufgestockt und der bisherige Innenhofbereich zwischen den beiden bestehenden Klassentrakten wird geschlossen und überdacht. Hierzu wird die nicht ausreichend tragfähige Spannbetondecke über dem nördlichen Klassentakt zurück gebaut und durch eine neue Stahlbeton-Massivdecke ersetzt. - Das neue Obergeschoss wird in vorgefertigter Holzbauweise mit tragenden Wänden als Massivholzkonstruktion bzw. Holzständerkonstruktion und oberster Geschossdecke als Brettsperrholzkonstruktion errichtet. - Die zentrale Aula wird mit einer Glasdachkonstruktion versehen. - Die Spannbetondecke im Flurbereich über dem bestehenden Kriechkeller des Nordtraktes muss durch Stahlträger ertüchtigt werden. - Kleinteilige Grundrissänderungen im Bestand - Die Pavillons werden entkernt und zur erweiterten überdachten Pausenhoffläche - Verbesserung des Wärmeschutzes sämtlicher Gebäudehüllflächen (Dachflächen, Fenster, hinterlüftete Holzfassaden, Kellerdeckendämmung) - Modernisierung der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung inkl. kontrollierten Lüftungseinrichtung mit Wärmerückgewinnung, energiesparender Beleuchtungssysteme, Gebäudeautomation, einschließlich der digitalen Anforderungen an Schulgebäude - Optimierung des Brandschutzes und Umsetzung des schulischen Schutzkonzepts

buyer: Brugg Regio, Regionalplanungsverband Brugg, Arbeitsgruppe Gesundheit
title: Mandat: Entwicklung, Umsetzung und Einführung der Versorgungsregion Brugg (Alters- und Langzeitversorgung) – Pilotprojekt
description:
Der Regionalplanungsverband Brugg Regio lanciert zusammen mit dem Kanton Aargau ein Pilotprojekt zur Entwicklung, Umsetzung und Einführung einer Versorgungsregion Brugg im Bereich der Alters- und Langzeitversorgung. Ziel ist der Aufbau einer koordinierten, regional abgestimmten Versorgungsstruktur in Zusammenarbeit mit der bestehenden Koordinationsstelle Alter, den Gemeinden sowie weiteren lokalen Akteuren, gestützt auf das Konzept für die Pilotphase und die Gesundheitspolitische Gesamtplanung des Kantons Aargau.

Die Leistungserbringung wird als Mandat ausgeschrieben.

Das Pilotprojekt dauert 3 1/2 Jahre.


Zentrale Punkte in der Ausschreibung

A. Leistungsbeschreibung

  • Entwicklung und Umsetzung eines Versorgungskonzepts für eine künftige Versorgungsregion Brugg
  • Aufbau der Zusammenarbeit mit der bestehenden Koordinationsstelle Alter und den weiteren lokalen Akteuren
  • Erstellen einer Meilensteinplanung
  • Erarbeitung eines Wegweisers für die Bevölkerung zur Versorgungsregion
  • Entwickeln eines Monitorings zur Versorgungsregion
  • Entwicklung und Führung von statistischen Grundlagen und weiteren strategischen Aufgaben
  • Beratung der Gemeinden und Akteure der Versorgungsregion
  • Stakeholder-Management (Gemeinden, Leistungserbringer, Kanton)
  • Verfassen von Stellungnahmen zu politischen Vorstössen und Gesetzesvorlagen
  • Berichterstattung gegenüber der Arbeitsgruppe Gesundheit und dem Vorstand von Regio Brugg
  • Planung einer Verankerung der Versorgungsregion und deren Organisation nach der Pilotphase oder Abschluss des Projekts



B. Projektziele & Meilensteine

  • Jährliche Evaluation des Projektverlaufs an den Vorstand von Brugg Regio
  • Periodische mündliche Berichterstattung und Diskussion des Projektverlauf mit der Arbeitsgruppe Gesundheit (=Projektsteuerung) von Brugg Regio
  • Meilensteine gemäss Konzept zur Pilotphase
  • Abbruch- oder Anpassungsklauseln


C. Governance

  • Die Vergabe erfolgt durch den Vorstand Brugg Regio auf Antrag der Arbeitsgruppe.
  • Brugg Regio führt die Buchhaltung für das Pilotprojekt, Budgetverantwortung beim Mandatsträger und Arbeitsgruppe.
  • Die Projektbegleitung wird durch die Arbeitsgruppe wahrgenommen.
  • In der Arbeitsgruppe ist eine Vertretung der Verwaltung, welche den Zugang zur Verwaltung der beteiligten Gemeinden sicherstellt und beratend für Verwaltungsabläufe zur Verfügung steht.

description: 1. Szczegółowy opis przedmiotu zamówienia określony został w umowie, której projekt stanowi załącznik do SWZ. 2. Produkty ICT, usługi ICT i procesy ICT 1) Zamawiający wymaga, aby oferowany przedmiot zamówienia, w tym produkty ICT, usługi ICT oraz procesy ICT wykorzystywane do realizacji zamówienia, zarówno jako elementy główne, jak i komponenty, elementy infrastruktury, elementy środowiska świadczenia usług lub rozwiązania towarzyszące, spełniały wymagania wynikające z obowiązujących przepisów prawa, w szczególności przepisów dotyczących cyberbezpieczeństwa. 2) Wykonawca zobowiązany jest zapewnić, aby produkty ICT, usługi ICT oraz procesy ICT wykorzystywane do realizacji zamówienia nie obejmowały: a) produktów ICT, usług ICT lub procesów ICT wskazanych w rekomendacji, o której mowa w art. 33 ust. 4 ustawy z dnia 5 lipca 2018 r. o krajowym systemie cyberbezpieczeństwa, stwierdzającej ich negatywny wpływ na podstawowy interes bezpieczeństwa państwa; b) produktu ICT, którego typ został określony w decyzji w sprawie uznania dostawcy za dostawcę wysokiego ryzyka, o której mowa w art. 67b ust. 15 ustawy z dnia 5 lipca 2018 r. o krajowym systemie cyberbezpieczeństwa, ani usług ICT lub procesów ICT określonych w tej decyzji. c) Wymaganie, o którym mowa w ust. 2, dotyczy produktów ICT, usług ICT oraz procesów ICT objętych ofertą lub wykorzystywanych do realizacji przedmiotu zamówienia, w zakresie, w jakim są one znane Wykonawcy na dzień składania ofert. 3) W szczególności za elementy ICT związane z realizacją przedmiotu zamówienia Zamawiający uznaje: a) systemy i oprogramowanie wykorzystywane do świadczenia usług telefonii komórkowej i usługi Centrum Krótkich Wiadomości Tekstowych (CKWT) – bramki SMS; b) systemy i oprogramowanie wykorzystywane do zarządzania usługami, kartami SIM/eSIM, numeracją, ruchem telekomunikacyjnym lub obsługą CKWT; c) urządzenia i komponenty infrastruktury telekomunikacyjnej wykorzystywane bezpośrednio do świadczenia usług objętych zamówieniem, jeżeli stanowią element oferowanego rozwiązania; d) karty SIM oraz eSIM; e) inne produkty ICT, usługi ICT lub procesy ICT wykorzystywane przez Wykonawcę do realizacji przedmiotu zamówienia, których zastosowanie ma istotne znaczenie dla świadczenia usług objętych zamówieniem. 4) Zamawiający nie wymaga wskazywania w wykazie, o którym mowa w pkt V SWZ dotyczącym przedmiotowych środków dowodowych, pojedynczych elementów infrastruktury operatora, które nie są możliwe do jednoznacznego przyporządkowania do realizacji przedmiotu zamówienia albo których wskazanie nie jest niezbędne do weryfikacji spełniania powyższych wymagań.

title: Germany – Liability insurance services – Bauherrenhaftpflichtversicherung für die vorgezogene Schadstoffsanierung des Gasteig – Teil 4: Höherdeckung (Exzedent) Beteiligtenversicherer
description: Der Gasteig ist das große, zentral gelegene Kultur- und Bildungszentrum Münchens. Mit ca. 1,8 Millionen Besuchern und mehr als 1.800 Veranstaltungen pro Jahr ist er das größte Kulturzentrum Deutschlands. Nach einer über 30-jährigen, intensiven Nutzungsphase steht die Generalsanierung des Gebäudes an. Vorgelagert wird in den Jahren 2027-2028 die Schadstoffsanierung des Gebäudes erfolgen.Die Münchner Raumordnungsgesellschaft mbH (MRG) als Auftraggeberin (AG) beabsichtigt die bedarfsgerechte Versicherung während der vorgezogenen Schadstoffsanierung / des Rückbaus des Gasteigs im Rahmen einer Bauherrenhaftpflichtversicherung. Die Beschaffung der Bauherrenhaftpflichtversicherung erfolgt in vier Teilen.Der Führungsversicherer für die Grunddeckung der Bauherrenhaftpflichtversicherung wurde bereits ermittelt und beauftragt. In einem zweiten Verfahren folgte für die Grunddeckung die Ermittlung des/der Beteiligungsversicherer/s für die Grunddeckung. Dieses Verfahren steht kurz vor dem Abschluss.Der Vertrag für die Höherdeckung (Exzedent) wird in zwei weiteren Verfahren ausgeschrieben. Das Verfahren für den Führungsversicherer für die Höherdeckung wurde ebenfalls bereits gestartet.Gegenstand des vorliegenden Verfahrens ist die Bauherrenhaftpflichtversicherung für die vorgezogene Schadstoffsanierung – hier hinsichtlich des/der Beteiligtenversicherers für die Höherdeckung (Beschaffungsteil 4). In diesem Verfahren wird der im ersten Beschaffungsteil im Wege der Verhandlung ermittelte Vertrag zu Grunde gelegt; eine Verhandlung über Vertragsinhalte findet nicht statt. Es wird ein sog. Nicht offenes Verfahren gem. § 16 VgV durchgeführt. Dieses Verfahren wird jetzt gestartet. Die vorläufige Kontraktsumme beträgt 59 Mio. EUR.Der genaue Leistungsgegenstand ergibt sich aus den gesamten Vergabeunterlagen, insbesondere der Police (Höherdeckung)– Vergabeunterlage D.01 nebst Anlagen sowie den Unterlagen zum Projekt – Vergabeunterlagen E_01.

title: Germany – Engineering services – 2026-07-lsvs-bogenhalle-technische-ausruestung
description: Die unter Denkmalschutz stehende Bogenhalle wurde in den Jahren 1950-1955 als Teil der Neubauten der Staatlichen Sportschule errichtet. Das Ensemble setzt sich aus drei Bauteilen zusammen: - die Sporthalle, die wegen ihrer typischen Bogensegmente als Bogenhalle bezeichnet wird - die Gerätturnhalle - das Eingangsgebäude mit den Umkleiden. 1977 wurde die Gerätturnhalle um einen schlichten Anbau aus einer Stahlhallenkonstruktion erweitert. 1980 wurde an der Gerätturnhalle eine sog. Schnitzelgrube unter Berücksichtigung der historischen Materialien aus Stahlbeton und Sandsteinfassade ergänzt. 1989 wurde am Empfangsgebäude eine weitere Halle aus Stahlkonstruktion als Schießhalle angebaut. Die Halle dient den Schützen als Übungsraum. Bis auf die Anbauten ist das Ensemble der Bogenhalle weitgehend unverändert im Originalzustand erhalten und steht unter Denkmalschutz. Die Installationen (Umkleiden, Nasszellen, Heizung, Lüftung) sind abgängig und müssen dringend erneuert werden. In einer vorlaufenden Untersuchung wurden Maßnahmen ermittelt, um den aktuell gültigen Energieverbrauch für Heizungen einhalten zu können. Neben der energetischen Sanierung der Außenhülle des Gebäudeensembles sind die sanitären Anlagen grundlegend zu sanieren und den aktuellen Anforderungen anzupassen. Die Außenanlagen sind nicht Gegenstand der geplanten Maßnahme. Ausnahme bildet der Zugangsbereich mit den Treppen und Rampen zum Empfangsgebäude. Hier sind insbesondere Betonsanierungen der Treppe erforderlich, sofern dies in einem wirtschaftlichen Rahmen und nach Überprüfung der statischen Erfordernisse sinnvoll ist. Eine denkmalrechtliche Genehmigung ist auf jeden Fall einzuholen. In der geplanten Maßnahme wird die Schießhalle nicht berücksichtigt. Die Sanierungsmaßnahme wird von der saarländischen Landesregierung gefördert. Nach einer ersten Kostenschätzung belaufen sich die voraussichtlichen Sanierungskosten auf 8 Mio. EUR brutto (Kostengruppen 300 - 700).

Im EG sind Gruppen- und Nebenräume für 60 Krippen- und im OG für 108 Kitakinder geplant. Für ca. 40 Mitarbeiter sind Sozial- und Nebenräume geplant. Im EG wird die Kitaleitung im nördlichen Gebäudeteil untergebracht, sowie ein Büro- und Kursraum für die Kiez-Arbeit. Der Haupteingang ist an dem Vorplatz zum Schwalbenweg hin angeordnet. Die interne Erschließung erfolgt über zwei innenliegende Treppenhäuser und einen zentralen Flur. Im Foyer sind sowohl im EG, als auch im OG die Mensen mit mobilen Trennwandsystemen geplant, welche auch für Aufführungen oder Versammlungen genutzt und in der Fläche erweitert werden können. Das Gebäude ist in massiver Bauweise als KS-Mauerwerksbau mit Stahlbetondecken und einer Holz-Satteldachkonstruktion im OG geplant. Über dem nördlichen eingeschossigen Gebäudeteil ist ein Stahlbeton-Flachdach geplant. Auf beiden Dachformen ist ein Gründachaufbau mit extensiver Begrünung als Warmdachkonstruktion vorgesehen. Die Fassade bekommt in Teilbereichen eine Vorhangfassade aus Holz und ansonsten eine Vorsatzklinkerschale mit entsprechenden Dämmungen. Weitere Informationen entnehmen Sie bitte den Vergabeunterlagen.

title: Germany – Environmental services – Biologisches Monitoring WRRL 2027 bis 2030 - Makrozoobenthos
description: Beauftragt werden biologische Untersuchungen des Makrozoobenthos (Probenahme, Bestimmung, Auswertung) zur Bewertung des ökologischen Zustands der Fließgewässer in Baden-Württemberg im Rahmen des biologischen Monitorings nach europäischer Wasserrahmenrichtlinie (WRRL). Das Untersuchungsgebiet umfasst ca. 880 Untersuchungsstellen, die teilweise zweimal zu untersuchen sind, sodass in einem Zeitraum von 4 Jahren (von 2027 bis 2030) insgesamt etwa 1.120 Untersuchungen durchzuführen sind. Dabei sind in den Losen 1 bis 6 in den Jahren 2027 und 2030 jeweils die gleichen Überblicksmessstellen zu untersuchen. Der Vertrag umfasst, neben der Probenahme der biologischen Qualitätskomponente Makrozoobenthos in baden-württembergischen Fließgewässern, die Bestimmung der erfassten Taxa, die EDV-technische Datenaufbereitung, die Auswertung und Bewertung der Daten, das Anlegen einer Belegsammlung zur Qualitätssicherung sowie zwei Besprechungstermine pro Jahr bei der LUBW in Karlsruhe.

title: Germany – Load-bearing structure design services – 2026-07-lsvs-bogenhalle-tragwerksplanung
description: Die unter Denkmalschutz stehende Bogenhalle wurde in den Jahren 1950-1955 als Teil der Neubauten der Staatlichen Sportschule errichtet. Das Ensemble setzt sich aus drei Bauteilen zusammen: - die Sporthalle, die wegen ihrer typischen Bogensegmente als Bogenhalle bezeichnet wird - die Gerätturnhalle - das Eingangsgebäude mit den Umkleiden. 1977 wurde die Gerätturnhalle um einen schlichten Anbau aus einer Stahlhallenkonstruktion erweitert. 1980 wurde an der Gerätturnhalle eine sog. Schnitzelgrube unter Berücksichtigung der historischen Materialien aus Stahlbeton und Sandsteinfassade ergänzt. 1989 wurde am Empfangsgebäude eine weitere Halle aus Stahlkonstruktion als Schießhalle angebaut. Die Halle dient den Schützen als Übungsraum. Bis auf die Anbauten ist das Ensemble der Bogenhalle weitgehend unverändert im Originalzustand erhalten und steht unter Denkmalschutz. Die Installationen (Umkleiden, Nasszellen, Heizung, Lüftung) sind abgängig und müssen dringend erneuert werden. In einer vorlaufenden Untersuchung wurden Maßnahmen ermittelt, um den aktuell gültigen Energieverbrauch für Heizungen einhalten zu können. Neben der energetischen Sanierung der Außenhülle des Gebäudeensembles sind die sanitären Anlagen grundlegend zu sanieren und den aktuellen Anforderungen anzupassen. Die Außenanlagen sind nicht Gegenstand der geplanten Maßnahme. Ausnahme bildet der Zugangsbereich mit den Treppen und Rampen zum Empfangsgebäude. Hier sind insbesondere Betonsanierungen der Treppe erforderlich, sofern dies in einem wirtschaftlichen Rahmen und nach Überprüfung der statischen Erfordernisse sinnvoll ist. Eine denkmalrechtliche Genehmigung ist auf jeden Fall einzuholen. In der geplanten Maßnahme wird die Schießhalle nicht berücksichtigt. Die Sanierungsmaßnahme wird von der saarländischen Landesregierung gefördert. Nach einer ersten Kostenschätzung belaufen sich die voraussichtlichen Sanierungskosten auf 8 Mio. EUR brutto (Kostengruppen 300 - 700).

title: Denmark – Electrical machinery, apparatus, equipment and consumables; lighting – EU-udbud vedr. levering, installation og drift af ladepunkter til egen flåde i Sønderborg Kommune
description: Sønderborg Kommune, herefter benævnt ”Bygherre”, er i gang med en løbende udskiftning af den nuværende fossildrevne personbilflåde til elbiler. Bygherre ønsker derfor at etablere en række ladepunkter dedikeret til disse køretøjer på forskellige lokationer i kommunen. Selve indkøbet af elbiler er ikke en del af nærværende udbud. Nærværende udbud vedrører levering, installation og idriftsættelse af ladepunkter til en del af Sønderborg Kommunes kommunale køretøjer. Derudover vedrører udbuddet alle nødvendige elarbejder mellem tilslutningspunktet og ladepunkterne, samt planlægning, projektering og udførelse af alle grave- og reetableringsarbejder, som er nødvendige for at etablere infrastrukturen. Slutteligt vedrører udbuddet også service og vedligeholdelse af ladepunkterne samt levering af en softwareløsning i en 5-årig periode med mulighed for forlængelse af to (2) gange ét (1) år. Det er for Bygherre vigtigt at indgå et samarbejde med en Operatør, som har forståelse for, at ladepunkterne er kritisk infrastruktur, da dele af den kommunale flåde er hjemmeplejebiler, som benyttes i en samfundsmæssig vigtig opgave. Sønderborg Kommune skal eje de indkøbte ladebokse og ladestandere mv. Derudover betaler Sønderborg Kommune tilslutningsafgifter og det løbende strømforbrug afregnes direkte med elselskabet. Kontrakten vedrører følgende 4 lokationer i Fase 1 (i alt 196 ladepunkter): • Omsorg og Udvikling – Hjemmeplejen Distrikt Nordals, Nørreled 31, 6430 Nordborg • Omsorg og Udvikling – Hjemmeplejen Distrikt Fjord, Skovgade 13, 6320 Egernsund • Omsorg og Udvikling – Hjemmeplejen Distrikt Sydals, Tandsbjerg 10B, 6400 Sønderborg • Omsorg og Udvikling – Hjemmeplejen Distrikt Alssund, Kongevej 19, 6400 Sønderborg Derudover er der følgende optioner: • Option 1 vedrører 2 lokationer (i alt 32 ladepunkter) • Option 2 vedrører 5 lokationer (i alt 26 ladepunkter) • Option 3 vedrører 2 lokationer (i alt 20 ladepunkter) • Option A vedrører 38 eksisterende ladepunkter, fordelt på en række lokationer, af mærket ABB, som Bygherre ønsker overgår til et samlet driftssystem, hvis muligt I udbudsmaterialet anvendes både betegnelserne ”Operatøren” og ”Entreprenør”. Disse betegnelser er synonymer i nærværende materiale, og betegner den vindende tilbudsgiver, samt dennes underentreprenører, der indgås kontrakt med. Der henvises i øvrigt til definitionsliste i Kravspecifikationen. Det udbudte arbejde er mere detaljeret beskrevet i udbudsmaterialet.
